在较高层面上，根据经验，Google 认为他们首先为 Google 规模的公司提供服务，然后再为人员规模提供服务。对于其他公司来说，情况恰恰相反。一般来说，这意味着您在第一次使用 Google 产品时会引导您通过 8 个不同的信息中心来设置 ACL，然后再雇用第二名员工。

At a high level though, as a rule of thumb Google assumes that they're serving companies at Google scale first, and at a human scale second. For other companies it's the opposite. My impression of anything enterprise (big or small) related to Google is that they just don't care / value solving it.

Which is sad, because "How does an enterprise customer pay for X?" is a non-trivial and incredibly important UX problem.

They have great technical solutions, but these are hamstrung by a frankly amateur understanding of how companies (startups to Fortune 500s) need to sign up, pay for, and track things.

From an outside perspective, one of the biggest gaps seems to be that internal Google product teams don't have to dogfood the full GCP et al. project/org experience. They get prebuilt billing structures (or just get to avoid them with internal cross-billing).

---

If I could waive a magic wand, Google would appoint an "Enterprise Czar", reporting directly to Pichai, who is a non-technical, retired founder / CEO.

That person would have one job: try to sign up, run (their team), and budget strategic Google initiatives (like AI) as a blind external party.

They would then deliver continuous reports to Pichai about how hard / easy this is.

Because potential Google customers don't give a shit if it's this internal team or that internal team's responsibility for integrating New Product X into GCP billing.

They care that the experience is terrible, filled with friction, and often flat out doesn't work.

fauigerzigerk 2026/08/14 15:57
我通常会同意这一点，但在这种特殊情况下，“每个人”只是 200 多人。他也可能原则上反对。

一次性追溯财富税是一种相当有问题的税收形式，即使你（像我一样）赞成寻找更有效地对超级富豪征税的方法。

当我读到这些一次性财富税时，我发现有一件事真的令人惊讶。一般来说，反对财富税的论点是，人们会改变自己的行为，随着时间的推移，这会减少税收。这当然是正确的。

但左翼经济学家认为，追溯性地实施这一政策并称其为“一次性”并不能改变人们的行为。从技术上讲，它无法改变他们对这一特定税收事件的行为。

但我发现，如果相信这种肇事逃逸的税收不会以其他方式改变人们的行为，从而减少税收收入，那就太天真了。

任何头脑正常的人都不会相信，一项在 5 年内带来 1000 亿美元收入的税收不必被同一群体或那些决定这样做的富裕群体支付的其他税收所取代。留下来。

I would normally agree with that, but in this particular case "everyone" is just over 200 individuals. And he could be opposing it on principle as well.

A one-off retroactive wealth tax is a rather questionable form of taxation even if (like myself) you are in favour of looking for ways to tax the super rich more effectively.

When I read about these one-off wealth taxes I find one thing really astonishing. The argument against wealth taxes in general is that people would change their behaviour, which would reduce the tax take over time. That's certainly true.

But then left wing economists believe that imposing it retroactively and calling it a "one-off" does not change people's behaviour. Technically, it cannot change their behaviour with respect to this specific taxation event.

But I find it utterly naive to believe that this sort of hit and run taxation will not change people's behaviour in other ways that would reduce tax revenues.

No one in their right mind would ever believe that a tax that brings in $100bn over 5 years will not have to be replaced by some other tax paid by the same group or by the somewhat less well off who decided to stay.
